clue.text: These guns satisfy more than one key requirement

definitions.meaning: first meaning: old muskets fired by a slow-burning cord

definitions.text: satisfy more than one key requirement
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as a phrase: what a key must do is fit locks, and fitting several is matching them

explanation.surface: Guns that tick several boxes for some important requirement.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as MATCH LOCKS: a key's whole job is to match its lock, and these do it for more than one.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchlock is an early firearm whose powder was lit by a smouldering slow match, so the plural names such guns.

clue.text: Faces Mercator made

definitions.meaning: first meaning: map is slang for a face
second meaning: the Flemish cartographer produced charts of the world

explanation.walkthrough: Mercator is the sixteenth-century geographer behind the familiar projection of the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Map is informal slang for a person's face, and charts of the earth were Mercator's work.

clue.text: For country, prepare to fire without hesitation

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: you train a gun on a target before firing
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: An order to a soldier to get ready to shoot for his country, without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: Without looks like 'lacking' but means outside: T(ER)RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Country in the sense of land or ground, its physical lie and features, is terrain.

clue.text: Flimsy construction made by eccentric MPs

parts.note: MPs sit in the House of Commons, known simply as the House
a work by someone is a work of theirs
an eccentric person is a card, so eccentrics are cards

explanation.surface: A shaky structure put up by some oddball members of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: MPs are Members of Parliament, who sit in the House; a card is British slang for a comic eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: A structure built of stacked playing cards collapses at a touch, so it stands for anything precarious.

clue.text: Confusing 12 with 26 can produce obstruction

indicators.note: confusing two things jumbles them together into a muddle

parts.note: the answer to 12 across
the answer to 26 across

explanation.surface: Mixing up two items can lead to a blockage.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle is something in the way, a barrier or hindrance blocking progress.

clue.text: Such a problem Alexander solved at a stroke

definitions.text: Such a problem Alexander solved at a stroke

parts.words: Such a problem Alexander solved at a stroke
parts.note: surface reading: a puzzle that a clever man cracked in one go; setter's reading: Alexander the Great cut the tangled Gordian rope with one sword blow

explanation.surface: A tricky problem someone called Alexander cracked in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: The legend says whoever undid the Gordian tie would rule Asia; Alexander simply cut it with his sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A knotty problem is a complicated, intricate one, and the legendary tie was literally full of tangles.

clue.text: Bareback, so to speak, in the ring

indicators.note: back asks for the word just found to be read from its end to its start
so to speak tells us to take Bare by its sound, as the animal word that sounds the same

parts.note: heard as bear back: the best-known bear in children's books is Winnie-the-Pooh, and back says to turn him round

explanation.surface: A circus act: riding horses without a saddle round the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Read Bareback as BEAR BACK: POOH the bear turned round gives HOOP. Bareback riders in a circus ring do leap through hoops, which keeps the surface honest.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoop is a circular band, so it is simply another word for a ring shape.

clue.text: Cover up what Matilda used to do?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to lie on top of something
second meaning, split in two: Belloc's Matilda told lies to excess

explanation.surface: A question about hiding the truth, as a famous liar did.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilaire Belloc's cautionary poem tells of Matilda, who told such dreadful lies; read the answer as OVER LIE, to lie too much.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlie is to rest on top of something, so concealing or covering it from above.

clue.text: Direct aim over empty space

parts.note: the point of something is its aim or purpose
a blank is an empty space on a form

explanation.surface: Pointing a gun straight across open ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, over places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A point-blank question or refusal is blunt and straightforward, which is what direct means here.

clue.text: Instruments for supersonic trip

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Musical instruments carried on a Concorde flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' reads as a journey but is the anagram signal on SUPERSONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Drums, cymbals and the like form the section of the orchestra played by striking.

clue.text: Endlessly observed one went to soldier's head

definitions.note: the headgear on a soldier's head

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: one kept, or observed, a rule or a festival
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone watched as a single thing went to a soldier's head, like success going to it.
explanation.walkthrough: KEPT loses its T, then I follows to make KEPI.
explanation.definitionFit: A kepi is the flat-topped peaked cap worn by French soldiers, so it sits on a soldier's head.

clue.text: Plant commonly said to make bird sing

definitions.note: a plant's name in common or dialect speech

parts.note: a sparrow is a bird
to sing is criminal slang for informing, as is to grass

explanation.surface: A herb that folk say will set a bird singing.
explanation.walkthrough: Sparrowgrass is the old folk corruption of asparagus. Grass and sing are both British slang for informing on someone to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Country speakers turned the vegetable asparagus into a familiar-sounding name for the same plant.

clue.text: Something for Holmes or Watson to handle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a crime or mystery for the detective to investigate
second meaning: Dr Watson is a physician, and a patient under treatment goes by this word

explanation.surface: A mystery waiting for Sherlock Holmes or Dr Watson to take on.
explanation.walkthrough: The two men are partners, but the clue splits them: one gets a mystery, the other, a doctor, gets a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter under investigation is a case, and so is a patient a doctor is treating.

clue.text: George symbolized 24 to religious group

parts.note: 24 across is gold, whose chemical symbol is Au
taken as written
pi is old slang for pious, religious
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: Someone called George stood for some cross-reference to a religious sect.
explanation.walkthrough: Symbolized signals the chemical symbol for 24, gold. George is British pilots' nickname for the automatic pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: In RAF slang George was the name given to an aircraft's automatic steering system, hence the nickname.

clue.text: Extremely hard — so simple I could be, without 29

indicators.note: could be suggests what the letters of so simple I might become when rearranged

parts.note: 29 is the country seat, read as bride's head: the first letter of bride, which so simple I lacks

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a task is very hard, though they claim it could be simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges SO SIMPLE I, but those letters are 'without 29': 29's answer, split as bride's head, is B, so B joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be done at all is the extreme of difficulty.

clue.text: Chap and I fail, lacking singleness of purpose

parts.note: a chap is a man
taken as written
a business that fails folds

explanation.surface: A man confesses that he and his partner both fail because they cannot decide what they want.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifold means many and varied, having numerous forms or aims, the opposite of single-minded.

clue.text: Author writes 24 before spring

parts.note: 24 across is gold, which is or in heraldry
a spring is a well, a source of water

explanation.surface: A writer composes something about gold before spring arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold here is the heraldic tincture, OR, a word crosswords lean on often.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell wrote Animal Farm and Nineteen Eighty-Four, so he is a famous author.

clue.text: Profit declared? Totally denied

parts.note: profit is gain
declared means said

explanation.surface: A company's reported earnings were flatly contradicted.
explanation.walkthrough: Totally works as a sum: profit plus declared, all added up.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is an old-fashioned verb for contradicting or disputing a claim, so its past tense means refuted.

clue.text: Mississippi river captain

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the river is nicknamed Ol' Man River in the song from Show Boat
second meaning: sailors call their ship's captain by this informal title

explanation.surface: The skipper of a Mississippi riverboat.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one riverboat captain, but the river itself and the captain are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The song Ol' Man River gave the Mississippi its nickname, and crews informally refer to a ship's master the same way.

clue.text: Non-participant seen at Twickenham

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who withdraws from a course or society
second meaning: a rugby restart kicked from the 22-metre line

explanation.walkthrough: Twickenham is the London ground that is the home of English rugby union, where a drop kick restarts play in this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who quits school or society is a dropout, and in rugby the term names a particular restart kick.

clue.text: Islander shows capability of officer

parts.note: a major is an army officer
being able to is what can expresses

explanation.surface: Someone from an island proves as capable as an army officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Capability of officer puts the officer's word first and the ability word after.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Majorca, the largest Balearic island in the Mediterranean, is a Majorcan.

clue.text: Writer to elect after constitutional reform

indicators.note: a reform reshapes something, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken letter for letter as material to rearrange

explanation.surface: An author called on to vote once the constitution has been changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Colette was the French novelist who wrote Gigi and the Claudine books.

clue.text: Monkey's silly mistake

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a loud-voiced American monkey
second meaning: a glaring, laughable blunder

explanation.surface: A monkey has made a daft blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: The howler monkey of Central and South America is named for its call, and a howler is also a ludicrous error.

clue.text: Paragon with nothing unusual to confess left witness box

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST, is a paragon of virtue
nothing is zero, the letter O
unusual means odd
to own up is to confess

explanation.surface: A model citizen with no secrets to admit steps out of the witness box.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusual looks like an anagram signal, but here it simply means ODD.
explanation.definitionFit: A witness who has finished giving evidence is said in court to have stood down from the box.

clue.text: Good standard in bull-ring

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ... standard, the benchmark of excellence
second meaning: in archery the innermost ring of the target, the bull, is coloured this and named after it

explanation.surface: Something of decent quality found in an arena for bullfights.
explanation.walkthrough: The bull-ring is not a Spanish arena but the centre of an archery target.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow centre of an archery target bears this name, and the metal is the proverbial benchmark of quality.

clue.text: Composer sounds like a natural music-maker

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is said the same as the word that follows

parts.note: a songbird makes music by nature

explanation.surface: A composer whose name evokes nature's own musician.
explanation.walkthrough: William Byrd was an English composer of Elizabethan church music.
explanation.definitionFit: William Byrd wrote masses and keyboard pieces in Tudor England, so he is a composer.

clue.text: Defect in obscure bit of writing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stain or flaw that spoils something
second meaning, a verb phrase: to smudge or blank out some words, as with ink

explanation.surface: A flaw hidden in a hard-to-read passage.
explanation.walkthrough: Obscure is a verb, not an adjective: the second meaning is to blank out some writing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a spot or flaw and a verb for spoiling or hiding writing with ink.

clue.text: Humorous speech from Liberal among rustics

indicators.note: among puts the one item inside the group named after it

parts.note: country folk taken together are the peasantry
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician cracks jokes while canvassing country voters.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside PEASANTRY, after the PE: PE(L)ASANTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasantry is a joking or polite remark, a bit of light good-humoured talk.

clue.text: Painter of Cockney girl

indicators.note: a Cockney Londoner famously drops the h at the start of words

parts.note: Hetty is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An artist who painted a London working-class girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the accent of working-class East London, which drops the H: HETTY becomes 'ETTY.
explanation.definitionFit: William Etty was a nineteenth-century English artist known for his nude figure studies.

clue.text: Country seat wedding-day close-up

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the great house of the Flyte family in Evelyn Waugh's novel
second meaning, split in two: a photograph framing the face of the woman being married

explanation.surface: A wedding photographer's close-up shot at a grand country house.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as BRIDE'S HEAD, it is just the shot a wedding photographer zooms in on. Brideshead Revisited is Evelyn Waugh's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Brideshead Castle is the stately home in Waugh's novel, and a stately home is an English country seat.
